$description: Bank UI Kit global design tokens — the single, platform-neutral source of truth. Format: W3C Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG). The scalar tokens here generate lib/src/theme/tokens.dart via `dart run tool/generate_tokens.dart`; CI fails if the two drift. Composite tokens (text styles, easing curves, shadows) remain hand-authored in Dart and reference these values. Per-brand theme tokens are exported separately to tokens/themes/ via BankThemeData.toJson (see test/theme_export_test.dart).

positiveBalance.$description: Positive balances on light surfaces (emerald-700, AA).

negativeBalance.$description: Negative / overdue amounts on light surfaces (AA).

pending.$description: Pending states on light surfaces (amber-700, AA).

positiveBalanceDark.$description: Positive balances on dark surfaces (emerald-400, AA).

negativeBalanceDark.$description: Negative amounts on dark surfaces (red-400, AA).

pendingDark.$description: Pending states on dark surfaces (amber-400, AA).

success.$description: System-level success feedback on light surfaces (emerald-700, AA). Unified with positiveBalance so one green family reads as "good" everywhere.

successDark.$description: System-level success feedback on dark surfaces (emerald-400, AA).

warning.$description: System-level warning feedback on light surfaces (amber-700, AA). Unified with pending.

warningDark.$description: System-level warning feedback on dark surfaces (amber-400, AA).

danger.$description: System-level danger / destructive-action on light surfaces (AA). Unified with negativeBalance.

dangerDark.$description: System-level danger / destructive-action on dark surfaces (red-400, AA).

investmentGain.$description: Investment gain on light surfaces. Same family as positiveBalance / success — one green per screen.

investmentGainDark.$description: Investment gain on dark surfaces (emerald-400, AA).

investmentLoss.$description: Investment loss on light surfaces. Same family as negativeBalance / danger.

investmentLossDark.$description: Investment loss on dark surfaces (red-400, AA).

creditAvailable.$description: Available credit headroom. Same family as positiveBalance / success.

creditUsed.$description: Credit already utilised. Same family as pending / warning.

networkMastercardBlend.$description: Mastercard brand mark: the overlapping-lens blend colour.

neutral.$description: The achromatic ramp every surface, ink, and border role is cut from. Ordered by luminance: 0 is white, 950 is near-black. Brands override the roles below, never the ramp.

surface.$description: Three surface tiers, light and dark. Light surfaces gain a tier from shadow, so base and raised share one white; dark surfaces gain it from lightness, because a shadow is invisible on near-black.

sunken.$description: The app canvas everything else sits on (neutral-100).

base.$description: Default card / tile surface, one tier above the canvas (neutral-0).

raised.$description: Sheets, menus, popovers floating above a card. Identical to base on light: the tier reads through the shadow, not a tint.

raisedDark.$description: Dark-mode floating surface (neutral-800) — lighter than base, because dark surfaces cannot borrow depth from a shadow.

ink.$description: On-surface ink tiers. Three levels of emphasis is the whole vocabulary — a fourth grey is how hierarchy turns to mud.

strong.$description: Primary ink: titles, amounts, body copy (neutral-950).

muted.$description: Secondary ink: captions, metadata, supporting copy (neutral-600, AA on surface.base).

mutedDark.$description: Dark-mode secondary ink (neutral-400, AA on surface.baseDark).

faint.$description: Tertiary ink: placeholders and disabled labels (neutral-500). Below AA for body text by design — never use it for content.

faintDark.$description: Dark-mode tertiary ink. The same mid-grey works both ways: it is the one rung equidistant from both canvases.

border.$description: Opaque outlines for components, and the translucent hairline used for rules between them.

outline.$description: Component outline: inputs, chips, unselected containers (neutral-200).

divider.$description: Rule between rows: primary ink at 8 % alpha. Translucent so it picks up whatever brand surface is behind it.

dividerDark.$description: Dark-mode rule: primary ink at 14 % alpha — low-luminance contrast compresses, so dark needs more alpha for the same perceived separation.

stateLayerHoverOpacity.$description: Hover state-layer opacity over interactive surfaces (M3-aligned).

stateLayerPressedOpacity.$description: Pressed state-layer opacity over interactive surfaces.

stateLayerFocusOpacity.$description: Keyboard-focus state-layer opacity over interactive surfaces.

disabledOpacity.$description: Opacity applied to disabled interactive content (M3-aligned).

focusRingWidth.$description: Stroke width of the keyboard-focus ring, in logical px.

focusRingOpacity.$description: Opacity of the primary-coloured keyboard-focus ring.

pressScale.$description: Scale applied to a pressable surface while pressed.

frozenCardSaturation.$description: Saturation multiplier for frozen card faces (desaturated, not greyed out).

opacity.$description: The alpha ladder. Every translucent tint and ink in the kit picks a rung here instead of inventing a decimal, so "a slightly stronger wash" is a step, not a guess.

faint.$description: Barely-there wash: card-face pattern inks, decorative tints.

subtle.$description: Hairline-strength wash: dividers on light surfaces, resting brand tints.

soft.$description: Resting fill of a tinted container (a brand-coloured chip or badge at rest).

muted.$description: Selected / pressed fill of a tinted container.

strong.$description: Emphasised tinted fill — the loudest a translucent brand wash gets before it should become an opaque colour instead.

scrim.$description: Half-strength: scrims behind modals, and ink that is deliberately recessive.

secondaryInk.$description: Supporting ink on a brand-coloured surface (card-face micro-labels), where a separate grey would fight the fill.

icon.$description: The icon-size ladder. Six rungs, each paired to a text role. The off-ladder 18 px and 22 px values still scattered through the widget layer collapse onto small/medium and medium/large respectively.

xSmall.$description: Inline with bodySmall / caption: chevrons and status pips inside dense rows.

small.$description: Inline with bodyMedium: leading glyphs in list rows and chips.

medium.$description: The default UI icon: list-tile trailing affordances, button leading icons.

large.$description: App-bar actions and primary controls (Material's own default).

xLarge.$description: Feature glyphs inside avatars, emblems, and quick-action rings.

hero.$description: Empty-state and success illustrations — the only rung that carries a screen on its own.

lineHeight.$description: Line-height multipliers. Every text style names a rung so vertical rhythm is a decision, not whatever metrics the loaded font happens to ship.

tight.$description: Hero numerals: a balance figure is one line, so leading is dead space.

snug.$description: Headlines and large numerals — display text that rarely wraps.

normal.$description: Labels, captions, and small numerals: single-line UI text.

tracking.$description: Letter-spacing for the cases that need it. Positive tracking is reserved for ALL-CAPS runs and grouped digits: on sentence-case text it looks loose, and it breaks cursive joining in Arabic script.

caps.$description: The standard ALL-CAPS micro-label (section headers, status pills) at caption / labelSmall size.

capsWide.$description: ALL-CAPS micro-labels on a card face, where the fill is large and the label needs to read as engraved.

numeralGroup.$description: Grouped digit runs — card numbers, reference and voucher codes — where the space is the grouping.

minTapTarget.$description: Minimum touch/tap target (WCAG 2.5.5 AAA / iOS HIG).

tileCompactBreakpoint.$description: Below this available width, metric tiles switch to their compact layout.

elevationTier.$description: The depth ladder, as ranks rather than pixels: which surfaces may sit above which. The shadow each rank resolves to is brightness- and brand-dependent (see BankThemeData.shadowFor), but the ordering is global, so a Figma frame and a Flutter widget agree on what floats over what.

flat.$description: Inset or flush surfaces, separated by a hairline alone.

floating.$description: Sheets, pickers, popovers — surfaces that overlay resting content.

hero.$description: Payment-card faces and feature banners: the one surface per screen allowed to sit highest.
